context.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to the Namibia Oil & Gas Podcast, your weekly gateway to the latest news and developments shaping Namibia's dynamic oil and gas sector. It's Friday, 28th August, 2026, and I'm Harrison Musimuko with the latest news, updates and insights from the Namibia oil and gas industry. Let's dive in. This week's top headlines. MIME endorses Namibia Local Content Conference and Exhibition 2026. Namibia-Nigeria Business Forum opens new pathways for trade and investment. Namibia strengthens global energy engagement at ONS in Norway. Recon Africa reports hydrocarbon flow to surface at Kavango West 1X. Hanwha Ocean takes on $4 trillion Namibia floating oil facility bid, backed by Green Strategy. Green expands Ilana Erasmus' role to lead oil and gas ICT strategy in Namibia. Equinox hopes to make a pretty big Namibia oil discovery. Every great industry begins with great people. Sixteen years ago, APOS made a commitment not just to recruit talent, but to build Namibia's future by investing in local skills, developing local professionals, and creating meaningful opportunities. We've helped shape the next generation of the offshore oil and gas workforce. Today, that vision becomes reality as our first group of Namibian professionals step into roles with leading international operators, proving that local talent can compete on the world stage. Africa Provider Offshore Services. Developing Namibian Talent. Powering Namibia's energy future. MIME endorses Namibia's local content conference and exhibition 2026. The Namibia Local Content Conference and Exhibition 2026 has received official endorsement from the Ministry of Industries, Mines and Energy ahead of its third edition, scheduled for 19 to 23 October in Vintuk. The endorsement strengthens institutional support for the conference, which is focused on increasing local participation, developing national capabilities and creating greater value for Namibian businesses across the country's resource sectors. Held under the theme Offshore Technology Innovation as a Pathway to Securing Namibia Local Content Development the Namibia Local Content Conference 2026 will bring together government industry investors service providers, and businesses to discuss skills development, supplier development, technology transfer, procurement, and innovation. With Namibia's oil and gas sector moving closer to major investment and development decisions, The conference aims to turn local content ambitions into practical opportunities for Namibian companies and professionals. Namibia Nigeria Business Forums opens new pathways for trade and investment. Namibia Nigeria are looking to deepen economic cooperation following the Namibia Nigeria Business Forum held in Vintook on 20 August 2026. The forum brought together government representatives, diplomats, and business leaders to explore opportunities for increased trade, investment, local content development under the African Continental Free Trade Area. Discussions highlighted several areas of potential cooperation, including petroleum and energy services, agriculture, logistics, infrastructure, and the digital economy. Nigeria's experience in natural gas, offshore operations, and technical oil field services was also identified as an area that could complement Namibia's growing energy sector, with participants stressing the need to move beyond dialogue and towards partnerships, investment, and tangible economic opportunities. Namibia strengthens global energy engagement at Offshore Northern Seas Summit in Norway. Namibia is strengthening its engagement with the international energy community as the Minister of Industries, Mines and Energy, Honorable Modestus Manushe, participates in the offshore Northern Seas Summit in Stavenger, Norway. The week-long event brings together government leaders, industry executives, and energy stakeholders to discuss oil and gas, energy security, technology, investment, and the future of the global energy sector. pending_qa.q: What strategic advantages does participation in the Offshore Northern Seas Summit provide for Namibia's energy sector development?
pending_qa.r: Participation in ONS provides an opportunity for Namibia to benchmark international practices, build strategic relationships, and gain insights that could support the development of its energy petroleum industry. As the country moves from exploration towards development, international platforms such as ONS are increasingly important for connecting Namibia with expertise, technology, investment, and partnerships across the global energy value chain.

pending_qa.q: What milestones has ReconAfrica achieved at the Kavango West 1X Discovery Well?
pending_qa.r: ReconAfrica and its partners BW Energy and Namco reported that natural gas and potential liquids are flowing to surface from two separate reservoir zones. The uppermost Huttenberg formation flowed hydrocarbons immediately after perforation, while the upper Ilanshok formation had previously demonstrated the ability to flow hydrocarbons to surface. ReconAfrica plans to conduct an open-hole horizontal production test targeting a lateral section of up to 1,000 meters.

pending_qa.q: What are the key technical features of Hanwha Ocean's FPSO design for Namibian offshore development?
pending_qa.r: Hanwha Ocean has secured approvals in principle from DNV and ABS for a low-carbon standard FPSO design, incorporating technologies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions. If selected for the Venus project, these technologies could be incorporated into the facility as Namibia's offshore development plans increasingly place emphasis on lower carbon production and emission management.

pending_qa.q: What services does Green Enterprises Solutions plan to provide to Namibia's emerging oil and gas sector?
pending_qa.r: Green Enterprises Solutions will provide turnkey ICT infrastructure to connect energy companies operating in Namibia with their international headquarters. Its services will cover connectivity, cybersecurity, data sovereignty, cloud integration, and scalable digital infrastructure alongside local technical support and training, becoming increasingly critical as Namibia's petroleum industry moves from exploration into development.

pending_qa.q: What is Equinor's recent entry strategy into Namibia's Orange Basin exploration sector?
pending_qa.r: Equinor recently agreed to acquire 17.4% participating interest in PEL90 from Hamilton Energy, a Chevron subsidiary, making the company's entry into Namibia's rapidly expanding exploration sector. The license provides Equinor with exposure to a drill-ready prospect with exploration activity expected in 2026.
